articleTitle: Treatment of Arbitrary-Shaped Boundaries with the Finite-Volume Time-Domain (FVTD) Method
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The use of unstructured meshes enables the Finite-Volume Time-Domain (FVTD) method to deal with arbitrarily-shaped boundaries. A selection of different boundary conditions that can be applied to surfaces is presented in this paper: dielectric interfaces, ports, perfect conductors and absorbing boundaries. The successful treatment of arbitrarily-shaped boundaries is proved on the basis of two examples. First the simulation of a corrugated horn antenna with the use of homogenized boundaries is presented. Second a broadband double-ridged horn antenna including oblique and curved surfaces is investigated. Both examples are embedded in computational domains with boundaries shaped to minimize reflections.

articleTitle: Spectrum Monitoring in China
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper outlines current spectrum monitoring situation, spectrum monitoring system, spectrum monitoring regulations, technical guidance, structure and function of monitoring networks in China. It provides other countries with 9 suggestions on how a country can monitor its radio spectrum better. With these suggestions, this paper puts forward some solutions on how to deal with relationship between national situation and ITU rules, how to deepen cooperation between monitoring agencies and other agencies, how to improve spectrum monitoring by technical management, how to deal with emergency interference and protect important frequencies.

articleTitle: Investigations on the Control of Microcontrollers Conducted Emission by Design
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with the conducted emissions induced by integrated circuits (ICs) operation on the power supply lines routed at printed circuit board (PCB) level. In particular, it describes a circuital model for an IC power supply net that makes possible to investigate the correlation between the power supply currents required by IC functional blocks and IC conducted emissions by performing SPICE simulations. The developed model provides a useful tool for digital IC designers in order to control of IC conducted emission in the earlier stages of the design.

articleTitle: Importance of Antenna VRP in Radiation Protection Consideration
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Compliance of radiation levels from transmitting stations with safety limits for general public exposure to electromagnetic fields (EMFs) is important issue in our times. Vertical radiation patterns (VRP) of the antenna systems are most important factor determining field strength distribution in area around transmitting station. Proper shape of VRP can minimise radiation and lead to conformity with limits given in regulations concerning radiation protection because of possibility of health hazard. In paper two examples of VRP modification on existing antenna systems has been presented. Such modernisation allows for substantial decreasing of radiation in area near transmitting station. VRP modifications were prepared by computer simulations and verify by measurements.

articleTitle: Theoretical Consideration for Real Time Observation of Dynamic Gravitational Fields Due to Earthquakes
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The possibility of observing dynamic gravitational fields generated by the time variation of mass density distribution due to earthquakes is discussed on the basis of a theoretical calculation of the dynamic gravity force generated by a model earthquake. The gravity force is evaluated at two locations. One is on the ground surface 100 km away from the hypocenter. Another is in the sky 100 km above the hypocenter. The calculation suggests that it will be possible to observe the dynamic gravitational field due to a big earthquake of the magnitude of about 6 at observation points 100 km away from the hypocenter, using a high-sensitive gravity sensor. If such observations will be realized, we will get new ways for preventing earthquake disasters, and besides observation of dynamic gravitational fields will open a new door to earth science.

articleTitle: Impact of the Base Stations Random Space Location in the Cellular Communication System on its Coverage Parameters
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Paper contains the analysis results of influence of the base stations (BS) space location randomness in the cellular communication system (CCS) on its coverage and responsibility parameters. The Probability curves of excess by the ratio of the BS responsibility zones areas in case of their both random and regular (ideal) location of a given level in percentage and the Probability curves of excess by the ratio of the BS coverage and responsibility zones areas in case of their both random of a given level in percentage for various kinds of network services, that require different levels of the BS signal exceeding the aggregate intra-network interference level at the subscriber's station location and in this regard application of various-dimension frequency clusters are present. Generally the network structure random nature demands an increase in the cluster dimension if compared to a regular structure to ensure the guaranteed communication quality, because the network non-regularity could lead to a loss of some of the services in a substantial part of this network's coverage zone with a reduction in this part of the zone of the signal-to-noise ratio to a value lower than the required to provide the corresponding services

articleTitle: An EMC Market Surveillance Project on Battery Chargers, Rechargeable Torches and Other Small Power Supply Units
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In 2003, The Safety Technology Authority of Finland (TUKES) organized EMC market surveillance tests on 22 battery chargers, rechargeable torches or other small power supply units. In this paper, the results are given and the lessons learned from this and TUKES's earlier projects are discussed. The project method proved to be a very suitable one especially with regard to EMC market surveillance. The projects produced important information with regard to the function of such a monitoring body as TUKES. It also brought to light problem areas in the field and potential failings or weaknesses in regulations and standards.

articleTitle: Impact of Electromagnetic Interference on QoS in Cellular Networks
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Influence of interference noises on GSM and GPRS QoS was experimentally measured and results of measurements are provided. These results indicate that actually received QoS in different places and for different users is different. Degradation of QoS is noticeable in zones where carrier over interference ratio (C/I) reaches the lowest acceptable level. For determination of C/I situation in the network two different methods are used: simulation and measurement. Both these C/I definition methods are not enough precise. In order to achieve high accuracy of C/I measurement we offer to carry out measurements involving all mobile stations (MS) in the network. We are analyzing what kind of changes should be made in the equipment of the user and the network in order to support this type of C/I measurement. Having collected C/I measurements from each network user and having correlated them with standard GSM measurements, it is possible to form a detailed and dynamically changing C/I matrix. This matrix would include information about all network users in their natural environment and C/I values would be measured quite precisely. While using this C/I matrix it is possible to indicate coordinates of low C/I zones quite easily and immediately proceed with means of interference reduction. Use of a precise C/I matrix, especially in heavily loaded networks, would make planning of the network and control of QoS easier. A C/I matrix can be also used for individual control of QoS of each user in the network.

articleTitle: Experimental Measurement and Validation of the Impact of Mobile Telephony on ERPS: A Preliminary Report.
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The aim of the present study was the gender related influence of electromagnetic fields on the P200 and N200 components of the ERPs. 19 normal subjects (10 women and 9 men) performed an auditory memory task both with and without exposure to a 900 MHz signal, emitted by a dipole antenna placed near the subjects’ head. The recordings of EEG and ERP signals were taken from 15 electrodes. At all the examined leads the amplitudes of N200 and P200 of women were greater than of men. Differences were more pronounced in the presence of EMF, especially at the frontal electrodes. (100 words)

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Emission of Complex Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Increasing demands on electromagnetic compatibility of electronic products require development of new circuit conception techniques. This is especially due to the demands on reduced emissions of microelectronic components in combination with higher complexity of electrical circuits. Looking at the postulation of decreased design cycles, this can only be achieved by simulations during the design phase which allow a prediction of the EMC behavior. Regarding the huge complexity of digital ICs (up to millions of transistors on one IC), it is necessary to develop electromagnetic emission models of single gates, functional units and also complete ICs (ASICs, microcontrollers, DSPs, etc.). Within this contribution a modeling methodology based on a bottom-up approach will be presented. It allows EMC analyses of whole VLSI-ICs during the design phase.

articleTitle: RFI Selection Criteria for New Radiotelescopes
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Man made Radio Interferences are still one of the major threats in the selection of sites suitable for the installation of new radio telescopes. The use of a mobile station to monitor spectrum occupancy can help in recognizing and identifying the most intense sources of interference, coming in particular from terrestrial transmitters. However many more actions should be taken in order to reach the level of radio quietness required by the class of new radio telescopes planned to become operational in the years 2010-2020. Planning for such measurement campaigns requires many trade-offs in order to collect, in a reasonable amount of time, a meaningful set of data, suitable to characterise each site. Finally even the interpretation of such database needs particular attentions because it could be easily misinterpreted by judgers a priori biased in favour of one site respect to the other.

articleTitle: Spectrum Management in Ghana: Challenges and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents the Spectrum Management approach in Ghana. It gives first a brief historic overview of telecommunication sector and the reasons that prompted the reformation of the telecommunication sector in the country. It outlines the problems and challenges facing the Frequency Management and Regulatory Body and identifies the socioeconomic benefits and opportunities that will come along with a stable enabling regulatory environment. Recommendations for the improvement of the telecommunication sector in Ghana are also given.

articleTitle: Analysis of Location Coverage Templates in Spectrum Monitoring
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper is, in fact, the second part of the paper “Methodology of spectrum monitoring network planning” at the same EMC WROCLAW 2004. Based on developed methodology for monitoring network planning and optimization, including determination of sets of location coverage subzones with known location uncertainties or accuracies, called “location coverage templates”, many such templates were calculated. The present paper gives analysis of template features for two, three and multiple monitoring/direction finding stations, separated by various distances and having different instrumental accuracies of bearing azimuths measurement.

articleTitle: Modeling of the Screens with Controllable Transparency
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with the problem of designing screens with controllable transparency at microwaves. Electromagnetic models of two constructions are discussed, both based on the integral equations application and their numerical solution. Key features of the designs are outlined.

articleTitle: Extraction of Critical Noise Propagation Paths in High-Density Interconnect Environment
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A straightforward solution to determine the distribution of transient noise within a circuit is based on simulation of all relevant interconnects including possible parasitic couplings. Such an approach requires initial knowledge on possible propagation paths as well as rather time consuming simulations. In contrast to this the method presented in this communication is based on the application of a recent and very efficient k shortest path algorithm to extract the critical propagation paths from a noise source to a specified integrated circuit input pin. The noise path tracing is performed considering all coupling phenomena between the transmission structures. The algorithm presented is illustrated by means of a transmission line circuit example.

articleTitle: Extremely Low-Intensity Electromagnetic Microwave as Corrector of Mammals Immunopatology
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: At present, the authors have elaborated on potential health effects of extremely low-intensity electromagnetic radiation focusing on it immunomodulative activity. In order to elucidate the new approach to noninvasive treatments that might result from exposure to microwaves, some animal models with modified immune status were developed. The goal of present study was to reveal the effects of fractionated (1.5h daily, for 30 days) exposure to low-density centimeter electromagnetic waves (8-18 GHz, 1 μW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) on immune system of animals with immunodepressive or immunostimulative animal model. The mice with the experimental tumors were used as model of an immunodepression. As other model that designs the changes in immune system activity, an antigenic stimulation of mice by foreign protein was provided. In present study, we have shown that MW exposure increased the adaptive response of an organism to tumor growth. Furthermore, we have discovered that prolonged irradiation of animals to centimeter waves increased antibody production to value, which had been reached only under the immunization with an adjuvant addition. The interpretation of results suggests that the exposure with centimeter low-level intensity electromagnetic radiation increases a resistance of an organism against tumor growth, and also gives a chance to be saved from the application of toxic adjuvants under immunotherapy.

articleTitle: The Scattering Fields Control by Reflective Type Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: New class of controllable reflective type antenna arrays is considered. These arrays are executed as integrated chips. The digital array probable states number is proportional to quantity of modules and each module allowable conditions number. This digital diffraction array has a set of microwave radar images. Such covers are capable to adapt for radartracking environment.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Wave Phenomena above Future Earthquake Epicentre by Satellite Monitoring Data
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The received by “Intercosmos” satellite data outcomes of electromagnetic response of a plasmasphere and upper ionosphere on processes of opening-up of earthquakes have confirmed existence. On the concrete example of November 23, 1980 earthquake dynamics (changes) of simultaneous time-space changes of plasma parameters of above zones of opening-up of earthquakes is analysed. The following parameters were analyzed (analysed): Intensity of low frequency noises in range 100 Hz - 20 kHz, Flow of vigorous electrons (Ee > 40 keV, Ee > 100 keV), Density and temperature of ambient satellite plasma. For complex analysis of variability of plasma parameters above an earthquake epicentre the data of ionospheric sounding (electron concentration) obtained simultaneously on “Intercosmos” satellite are involved (attracted). The changes of parameters of plasma at the upper ionosphere altitudes start some day (one or two) before the maiden (first) underground shock. Then sharp increases of low frequency emission intensity some hours (3-6 hours) before event are started above the future epicentre of earthquake. The dimensions of bursts observation zone are ±3° on a latitude and ±60° on longitude. 1.5-2 hours prior to impact (stroke) is watched narrow-band (2-3°) precipitation of vigorous electrons. The plenty of earthquakes cases were is parsed. It was established, the observation zones (registration) of seismoionospheric anomalies at altitudes of the upper ionosphere are determined and the scheme of temporary development of geophysical phenomena accompanying development of seismic danger is constructed. The set (combination) of researche outcomes of waves and plasma parameters by the “Intercosmos” satellite data allows to consider (count), that the processes registered on altitudes of the upper ionosphere and plasmasphere are the indicator of definite processes in lithosphere The method of global satellite monitoring of natural low frequency emissions in a complex with simultaneous measurements of parameters of ambient plasma (density and temperature of plasma) and flows of vigorous electrons is offered. The method realization will be useful not only to increase of an effectiveness and accuracy of the global control of environment near-earth space plasma, but also for forecasting (prediction) of earthquakes.

articleTitle: Atmosphere Radio HF Precursors of Earthquakes
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: During 1992-1995 the new kind of radio HF earthquake precursors are recorded simultaneous by the four electromagnetic stations a few days prior the event associated with earthquakes with magnitude more than 5.0 at Crete island. The specific peculiarities are found. First is under horizon epicenter position for observations of most important events under question. Second unusual result is conclusion that such preseismic HF signals (40-55 MHz) are responsible mainly for seaquakes. We made conclusion about developing thunderclouds activity before the seismic event. As result of our analysis of a number of continuous observations on a network of Crete island we can assume, that in an atmosphere above the sea on the eve of earthquake at heights of 0.1-10 km the electrically active clouds are produced and the conditions for the electrical discharges in an atmosphere are created which can serve a source of HF radio-emission registered on Crete. We suppose mechanisms of thunder electricity generation. It is the model of convection carrier that is started in an atmosphere by a horizontal gradient of temperature. It is proposed that the occurrence of electrical charges on a surface of the sea and transportation them further on heights up to 10 km in our model occurs due to pollution energy allocated within bottom of the sea as gases and heat injection. The power estimation of HF precursor was made for Crete net situation to compare with published HF data.

articleTitle: On Some Aspects of Using Tweek Atmospherics for Monitoring of the Lower Ionosphere
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A possibility of monitoring regular changes of the lower ionosphere height using night-time (tweek) atmospherics is demonstrated in this study. To infer source range and ionosphere height we employed a technique based on modal interference properties of tweeks. An ensemble of three-component records (vertical electric and two orthogonal horizontal magnetic) obtained from board of a scientific vessel at different points of Atlantic and Indian oceans and during different moments of local night was used for analysis. Results of analysis show gradual changing of the ionosphere height during night time on a few kilometres with maximum reached at vicinity of the local midnight.

articleTitle: The Activation of Natural Killer Cells from MICE Subjected to Low-Intensity Extremely High-Frequency Electromagnetic Irradiation
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It was established that total body exposure of mice with millimeter waves caused a significant enhancement of natural killer cell cytotoxity after 24 hs exposure (exposure time ranged from 5 to 96 hours). The NK cell cytotoxity has been returned to normal level 24 hours after the cessation of exposure. The stimulation in NK cell activity was observed after exposure to millimeter waves both in vivo and in vitro. The possible mechanisms of millimeter wave effects are discussed.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Analysis of ALFVÉN Waves in a Uniform, Gravitating Medium
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Following the nonlinear Fourier analysis of Callebaut [1]-[6] we studied the stability of a uniform, gravitating medium pervaded by a homogeneous magnetic field. We found three totally different situations with our method of combined variable. (a) Alfvén waves, incompressible medium: full arbitrariness of either the perturbed velocity or the magnetic field provided the Alfvén dispersion is satisfied. (b) Alfvén waves, compressible nongravitating medium: dispersion relation OK but zero convergence for higher order terms. (c) Alfvén waves, compressible gravitating medium: nonlinear analysis possible.

articleTitle: Validation of Field Computation Results for Reverberation Chambers
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Computer simulation is a tool commonly used for predicting and explaining the electromagnetic behavior of technical structures. The validation of results prior to use them as basis for decisions is an important but not always an easy task. Often, results cannot be compared with results obtained by an independent method, such as measurements or analytical solutions. In such cases, consistency of results, and the fulfilling of boundary conditions is a good indication whether results can be trusted. In this paper a number of fundamental electromagnetic and physical principles are scrutinized in order to gain confidence in the results. In particular Ampere's law is used to check consistency between the current through a wire and the surrounding magnetic field; the electric field inside and outside a wire cage and the orientation of the electric field in respect to the exciting source is examined; and the relation between the difference in the energy stored in the electric and magnetic field during once cycle and the reactive power delivered by the source is evaluated.

articleTitle: Statistical Analysis of Measured Power Quality Indices in Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The quality of electric power supply is one of the most important aspects of EMC. The process of deregulation in transition countries as Croatia has great influence on the power (distribution) networks quality indices and the relations between electric power suppliers and end users. For that reason, it is very important to know power quality indices of power supply network. In this paper, measured results for all power quality indices, according to the European norm 50160, are presented. Measurements were performed on several (30) transformer stations with domestic, public and industrial consumers. The latest state-of-the-art power network analysers (MEMOBOX 800 and TOPAS 1000, supported by powerful mathematical software) were used for measurements and analysis.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of High-Frequency Components with the Use of Spatial Subgridding Techniques
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A study of FDTD solutions on variable, 2:1 and and 3:1 spatially subgridded meshes is presented. A mathematical study of numerical reflections for 2:1 and 3: 1 spatially subgridded FDTD schemes are proposed. Mathematical predictions are confirmed by simulating sections of parallel-plate line and rectangular waveguide.

articleTitle: A Method for Detection of Regional High Fissuring Zones and Lithospheric Deep Faults Using Ground-Based Magnetic Stations Data
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We have found that some largest deep faults of the terrestrial lithosphere manifest themselves in the horizontal component of the Earth's magnetic field. We have compiled a databank of magnetic stations located outside the lithospheric deep faults using the geological data. Every two chosen magnetic stations must be located nearly on the same corrected geomagnetic latitude, but above different tectonic zones. One of them should be located above the lithospheric deep fault and the other - outside a zone of deep faults. The horizontal geomagnetic field components measured at these stations were compared with each other. It has been shown that horizontal geomagnetic field components at the magnetic station, located above the lithospheric deep fault is much larger, than at the station, located outside the deep faults zone. The analysis of the horizontal geomagnetic field components measured over a large number of different tectonic regions has shown that the above mentioned characteristic is quite persistent. On the basis of the found regularities in the horizontal geomagnetic field component we propose a method for a detection of regional high fissuring zones and lithospheric deep faults. We compared the locations of the deep faults found by our method with those determined from other methods, namely by means of the satellite measurements of low frequency emissions and of the tectonic mapping and obtained good agreement between locations found by the three methods. The proposed method does not require any considerable investment, since the available world network of magnetic stations can be used.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Charge Transferred by Lightning during Catalonia (Spain) Thunderstorms
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Knowledge of lightning parameters related to electrical atmospheric discharges are essential to predict the severity such as over voltages in power lines or other damages. Today the availability of statistical data related to lightning is still important in order to infer the severity of particular situations such as an engineering design. One of the lightning parameters useful for engineering is the total electric charge related to the entire flash. This paper presents estimations of the total charge deposited by lightning as a result of the analysis of the electric field changes due to lightning.

articleTitle: Ecological Characteristics of Cellular Network: Relationship with its Radio Frequency Resource and Intrasystem EMC
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Paper contains the basic ideas and thesis's allowing to prove the limitations set on the quantity of cellular network operators and the volume of radio frequency resource allotted for every cellular radio network aimed at ensuring all the acceptable ecological characteristics of each radio network and determining the relation of cellular radio network ecological characteristics and those of its intrasystem (intranet) EMC. Possible ways of improving the ecological characteristics of cellular radio networks related to the limiting use of radio frequency resource and marginally accepted space density of the base network stations and the development and optimization of the methods and algorithms of the intranetwork EMC maintenance have been formulated. On the whole the systematic considerations of the cellular network ecological characteristics, suggested in the paper, helps the quantitative determination of their relation with the capacity and quality of the radio frequency resource, dedicated to a network, parameters of the intranetwork EMC, as well as to formulate a number of trends to improve the cellular network ecological compatibility.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Exposures by Cellular Phones on Aquatic Ecosystems Behavior IN-VIVO
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Result of measure the EMFs emitted by cellular phones on the behavior of aquarium fishes are presented. The registration of video-signals derived from animals activity and automated treatment, based on the fractal analysis of time series is offered.

articleTitle: Automation of Radiated Susceptibility Testing
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper describes the automation of radiated susceptibility test RS103 of MIL-STD-461E. The test software has the provision of swept frequency scanning and stepped scanning in open loop mode. Power requirement table, for specified field strengths, could be created automatically over the range of frequencies, for a particular step size, through closed loop system. Later, the table will be called back while testing by using swept frequency / stepped scanning in open loop mode. This technique reduces the time taken for setting the power level to establish constant field strength over the range of frequencies. Visual Basic and MS Access has been employed for developing the software in the Windows environment.

articleTitle: Comparison of Different Reverberation Chamber Geometries and Excitations Using a Frequency Domain Method of Moments Simulation
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper the simulation of reverberation chambers, which have different sizes, geometries, and excitation antennas is presented. Three-dimensional electromagnetic full wave simulations are carried out in the frequency domain using an electrical field integral equation based method of moments approach. An overview on the modeling procedure of the reverberation chambers and the excitation sources is given. The effect of a change in size, design form, or excitation of the chamber on the electric field pattern and on typical reverberation chamber performance parameters is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Test Stand to Investigate of Electromagnetic Influence as Side-Channel Attack on Stream Crypt-Device
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper author has considered an electromagnetic influence as side-channel attack. For this purpose the Test Stand, as well as tested stream crypt-device have been developed. The detailed information about the developed hardware has been discussed. 8-bit LFSR was chosen as a basic component of ciphering device in order to use the previously obtained statistical information and to simplify the investigation. The results of the investigation will allow to increase the resistance of the cryptology systems to EM side-channel attack.

articleTitle: Atmospheric Electric Field Distribution in the Surroundings of Buildings Having Lightning Protection Rods with/without Circular Loop
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Atmospheric electric field distribution in the surroundings of building having lightning protection rod with and without horizontal circular loop (Yugoslav national standard JUS N.B4.811) is determined in this paper.

articleTitle: ITU Spectrum Monitoring Studies
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Within ITU-R, Study Group 1 (SG1) is dealing with spectrum management in general. The scope of SG1 is defined as: Development of principles and techniques for effective spectrum management, sharing criteria and methods, techniques for spectrum monitoring and long-term strategies for spectrum utilization and economic approaches to national spectrum management as well as, in association with the appropriate bodies of the ITU, facilitation of the collection and dissemination of information concerning computer programs prepared for the implementation of relevant Recommendations. Within SG1 Working Party 1C (WP1C) is tasked with all matters related to spectrum monitoring. For the study period 2003-2007 WP1C has developed a new working programme, in which the various activities to be undertaken by WP1C are specified.

articleTitle: An Automated, Integrated Spectrum Management and Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Automated spectrum management and monitoring systems are available to support, simplify and automate many of the responsibilities of administration of the radio spectrum. Functions which can be automated include processing applications for radio service, assigning frequencies and issuing licenses; collection of fees for use of the spectrum; parameter measurement, occupancy and most other monitoring measurements; and detection and clearance of interference. The International Telecommunication Union recommends that spectrum management and monitoring systems be fully integrated. An integrated system can perform valuable functions including Automatic Violation Detection, where license information in the management system database and measurements from the monitoring system are used to identify unlicensed transmitters and transmitters operating outside of their licensed parameters.

articleTitle: Monitoring of Interference to the Cospas-Sarsat Satellite System in Canada
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The Cospas-Sarsat system was initially developed under a Memorandum of Understanding signed in 1979 by Canada, France, Russia and the USA to detect and locate potential survivors of an aircraft crash or maritime distress event. The system was first used operationally in September 9, 1982 with the rescue, in Canada, of three people from the crash of a light aircraft. Since 1982 the Cospas-Sarsat search and rescue satellite system has provided location information to rescue services searching for people in distress as a result of either an air plane crash, boat sinking or land-based emergency. It has been estimated that this worldwide satellite system has been responsible for assisting in saving of more than 14,250 lives during the 23 years of operation from 19822001 [1]. Unfortunately, the 121.5 MHz frequency band used in this system is being subjected to interference from sources such as consumer products, unauthorized communication devices, and industrial equipment. These interference sources have caused Cospas-Sarsat system false emergency reports. Recently, Canada has been experiencing numerous false alerts in some of its major cities. This paper presents the methodology for the characterisation of these interfering signals and examines the possible signal sources.

articleTitle: Plasmoid Tornado
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: HF discharge was created and studied in rotated and non-rotated airflow. Gas dynamic and plasma parameters were measured in plasma vortex generated by HF discharge in rotated airflow. Calorimetric measurements in gas flow behind plasma vortex were obtained. Extra power release about 400% was measured in this experiment. DC plasma power supply is created by plasma vortex. It is possible to use this DC energy. Probably natural tornado can generate such high electric field and high- energy electron beam in its head (down) part by the same mechanism. So, plasma vortex study in laboratory may be useful to study of natural tornado physics also.

articleTitle: Radio-Quiet Zones: National and International Perspectives
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Powerful new radio telescopes of the twenty-first century will have the ability to detect radio emissions from the earliest galaxies in our Universe. These faint clues to our origins reach Earth at frequencies outside the frequency bands officially allocated for radio astronomy. In order to detect these signals, new means will have to be found to mitigate the effects of human-generated interference. One way to do this is by establishing radio-quiet zones. A review is given of existing and planned radio-quiet zones.

articleTitle: Observations and Measurements of Broadband over Power Lines in the USA
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper summarizes the results of observations and measurements of Broadband over Power Lines (BPL) test sites in the Eastern USA. Of particular interest is the potential interference from BPL systems to MF/HF/VHF receivers in amateur stations located in residential areas.

articleTitle: A Technique to Reduce Electromagnetic Field Radiated by Indoor PLC Systems
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper proposes a technique aiming at reducing significantly the electromagnetic field radiated by indoor PLC signals, while not affecting the PLC signal itself. The basic idea is to take advantage of the additional ground conductor and inject a signal similar to the PLC signal into the ground-neutral line, but with a reversed phase. As a result, both the overall antenna mode- and transmission line mode-currents are significantly reduced, as well as the radiated electromagnetic fields. Numerical simulations obtained using NEC (Numerical Electromagnetics Code), as well as experimental measurements are also presented. It is shown that the proposed technique allows for a significant reduction (up to 20 dB) of the PLC electromagnetic radiation in the considered indoor frequency range (10-30 MHz).

articleTitle: Response of Plasmasphere to Earthquakes and Other Lithosphere Processes by Satellite Data
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The review of satellite experimental outcomes of registration of electromagnetic wave phenomena in the Earth plasmasphere and accompanied modifications of plasma parameters above epicentres of the future earthquakes is given. The response of a plasmasphere on fast (seismogenic) and slowly geodynamic processes in lithosphere is demonstrated. The possibility of using of the satellite data for prediction of catastrophic earthquakes is showed. The complex (integrated) research of results of satellite measurements of parameters has allowed to establish a pollution of the environment.

articleTitle: Regulatory Aspects: Directives, Standards and Specifications in EMC
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The presentation will describe the legal aspects of electromagnetic compatibility. Especially European regulations will be analyzed, among others the provision of Council Directive 89/336/EEC of 3 May 1989 on the approximation of the laws of the Member States relating to electromagnetic compatibility and the importance of EMC regulation for the proper functioning of the Internal Market (free circulation of goods - elimination of additional restrictions, principal of mutual recognition and technical harmonization). A special attention will be paid to the compliance of Polish legislation with European rules. A separate section will be dedicated as well to the role National Regulatory Authority plays in this field and legal instruments it has at its disposal.

articleTitle: Hybrid MMPO Method Combined with Z-Matrix Interpolation for Broadband Analysis of Scattering and Radiation Problems
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, method of moments combined with physical optics is proposed for broadband analysis of electrically large radiating/scattering structures. To improve efficiency of this hybrid method, impedance matrix interpolation technique is employed. Various Z-matrix interpolation schemes are discussed and compared as regards accuracy, computer memory requirement and speed up of calculations. Some results exemplifying usefulness of presented approach are shown.

articleTitle: One Radio Channel Packet Implementation Interference Analysis
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The wireless connection mode is quite perspective in rarely settled rural areas with the customer premise telecommunications network. One of the most popular wireless technologies is IEEE 802.11b. Our research of IEEE 802.11b equipment implemented in untypical conditions enables us to make the following conclusions: The interference of the CPN nodes significantly decreases the throughput and the capacity of the system. The CPN capacity may be significantly increased by organizing the transmissions of the frames implementing the dynamical space/time division, creating the running frames waves through the node chains. This article deals with the interference allocation of space/time hyper-plane in the dynamic one radio channel packet implementation. The principles of engineering of the customer premise’ networks and control of the space/time division approach, which ensure the electromagnetic compatibility and maximizes the network throughput, are researched.

articleTitle: Effective Method for Identification of Numbers of Telephone Lines to Which the Cordless Telephones Operating in GSM Frequency Bands are Connected
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a method, which enables to identify the number of the telephone line to which the illegal cordless telephone is connected. Usually the operating frequency band of illegal telephone is outside of the intended frequency bands. The use of this method in Vilnius radio monitoring station for one year, proved its’ effectiveness and greatly increased the number of identified illegal phones.

articleTitle: Lightning Transients in Telecommunication Cables Which Crosses with High Voltage Overhead Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents the mathematical model for the prediction of transients induced in underground telecommunication cables during direct lightning stroke on the grounding wire of high voltage HV overhead transmission line. Different places of crossing and different distance between towers and telecommunication cables were analysed.

articleTitle: “New” Radio Astronomy and a New Generation of Radio Telescopes
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The worldwide radio astronomy community is working towards the construction of a small number of radio telescopes with unprecedented large sizes, of up to one square kilometre in total collecting surface, and sensitivities that will surpass those of the largest operational instruments by up two orders of magnitude. The present goal is putting three instruments into operation in the timeframe 2008-2016: the Low Frequency Array (LOFAR) in the 10-240 MHz frequency range, the Square Kilometre Array (SKA) in the 150 MHz-22 GHz range and the Atacama Large Millimetre Array (ALMA) in the 31-950 GHz range. Their main scientific goals include probing the epoch of formation of galaxies and large-scale structures in the early Universe, through the observation of radio spectral lines at frequencies that are much lower (up to a factor of about 10) than their rest frequencies. This implies that these instruments will need to be able to operate outside the bands allocated to the radio astronomy service - although they will not need access to all frequencies all the time, they may well need access to all the frequencies some of the time. For this purpose, they will need to be made robust for radio frequency interference and beside this, regulatory aspects of their successful operation, like the definition of radio quiet zones, need to be studied.

articleTitle: Why are we Afraid of Electromagnetic Field ?
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The influence of the electromagnetic filed on organisms, as well as on technical equipment raises a lot of controversies. Protests against radio communication and power line investments have become very common. In the following paper the author analyses the attitudes toward the potential threat, discusses facts and myths about electromagnetic radiation, as well as presents “means of protection" and explains their miraculous properties.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Emissions from ARC Welding
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electric arc welding is accompanied by high- frequency electromagnetic emissions caused by the power source and by the arc as well. To distinguish to which extent the disturbances arise from the operation of the applied electronic power source and from the arc, alternatively to a welding inverter the arc was fed from batteries. Based on detailed investigations of the transition periods at the beginning and at the end of short-circuiting droplet transfer periods in SMAW and MAG welding, this type of metal transfer proved to be the reason for the relatively high radiated emission levels of these welding processes.

articleTitle: Idea and Design of Modulating Generator and Synchronous Receiver for Multi-Channel MST System
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Time consumption is a very serious problem of the electromagnetic field measurement. The authors have proposed a new design of measurement setup that allows solving the problem effectively. This aim can be obtained using a Modulated Scatterer Technique (MST) with simultaneous modulation of an array of scattering probes and multi-channel synchronous detection. In the paper an idea and design of the modulating generator and synchronous receiver for a multichannel MST system is described.

articleTitle: Studies on the Influence of the PLC Signal on Other Telecommunication Systems
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes some studies on the influence of the power line communications on other telecommunications systems in terms of radiated electromagnetic field, conductive coupling within the equipment, and inductive coupling between power and telecommunications lines. Distribution of common mode impedance and the longitudinal conversion loss were obtained from in-situ measurement in Japan. The effects of conductive and inductive couplings on VDSL systems were investigated.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Fields and Schumann Resonance on Taiwan Earthquakes
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: There are two kinds of method to estimate precursory phenomena of the earthquake using electromagnetic wave. One of them is measuring direct wave near from the ground surface of the epicenter (direct method). ULF/ELF electromagnetic wave is used because propagation loss is very low. Another one is measuring the change of the intensity or phase of electromagnetic wave from a transmitting station reflected at the ionosphere (indirect method). These fluctuations are understood as a change of ionosphere that disturbed by the energy from the epicenter. VLF/VHF electromagnetic wave is used in order to observe electromagnetic wave of transmitting station. These two kinds of technique are very different each other about observation place, observation system, and analyses method. We have carried out our observation of ELF electromagnetic wave below 50Hz at Nakatsugawa in Japan (Geographic lat. 35° 25 ' N, long. 137° 33' E, Geomagnetic lat. 25° 05' N in Gifu Prefecture near the foot of Mt. Ena) where the electromagnetic environment is good. In this frequency band, we tried to observe ELF electromagnetic wave and the fluctuation of ionosphere using Schumann resonance.

articleTitle: Criteria of Choice of Mode Stirred Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The recent publication of the standards RTCA DO 160 [1] and EN 61000-4-21PR [2] modify the status of the mode stirred reverberation chambers. The test facilities were experimental. Today they are industrial and recognized. To design a mode stirred chamber, it should take into account several criteria which influence the performances. The dimensions of the reverberation chamber and the size of the mode stirred influence the statistic uniformity and the frequency bandwidth. Nevertheless shielded enclosures with identical dimensions are able to generate different fields in function of the way they are manufactured. To reach high field, it is necessary to use low surface shielding technology, to obtain sufficient shielding effectiveness and to use the correct materials.

articleTitle: The New GSM-Like Exposure System
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Biomedical experiments with investigate possible effect arising from handheld terminals as GSM mobile phones must deploy an excitation field witch matches the true situation. Complex amplitude-phase modulation from digital TDMA handheld terminals generated much more complicated than just EM fields bursting of RF field with certain repetition rate and duty cycle. In experiments with model of handheld phones we have to pay attention not only on RFEMF, but also on ELF magnetic field connected witch the current burst powered power amplifier, too. The H-field intensity was estimated for several types of portable devices and then confirmed on experimental way. A new exposure system was proposed that allow to expose an object simultaneously to HF EMF and LF H-field equivalent to the modulation system.

articleTitle: A Circuit Model for Polymer Transient-Voltage Suppressor
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A circuit model for polymer transient-voltage suppressors has been described. Employing this model, circuit simulation studies have been carried out to determine the response of the transient suppressor to Human Body Model (HBM) Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) transient. The model would be useful in the study of off-chip ESD protection for RF and high-speed digital circuits.

articleTitle: Adding CDMA Capabilities to the Seamcat Spectrum Engineering Analysis Tool
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes recent developments of the SEAMCAT tool, the spectrum engineering tool jointly developed and used in CEPT. In particular, the paper describes how the new functionality of modelling the land mobile systems based on CDMA technology will be implemented.

articleTitle: Lightning Verification of Airborne Systems - Comparison of Test Set-Ups
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: For lightning verification of aircraft, certification authorities require to determine the voltages and currents to which aircraft wiring and avionics equipment are exposed. Theoretical investigations are not accepted by the authorities as a sole means of validation. Those analyses have to be supplemented by test results of actual measurements. To perform those measurements the certification authorities of some countries insist on a cost intensive test set-up which is known as „Coaxial Return Line“, other countries are not requiring complete system tests but just equipment tests. Due to the fact that current aircraft use more and more composite components (CFC) for structural parts of the aircraft while the number of electronic/electrical equipment with critical functional modes is increasing, the certification efforts and costs become very expensive. Therefore the question arises, whether it would be possible or even more adequate to return to the less cost intensive test set-up, the so-called „Single Return Line“. This paper highlights the differences of the above mentioned test methods from a physical point of view. Actual test results with both test set-ups on a real composite aircraft (a helicopter) support the theoretical assumptions, and clarify the applicability of more simple test set-ups.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Sensor Method for EMC/EMI Analysis in Severe Electromagnetic Environment Using EMC-Analyzer Expert System
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Abstract This paper suggests a method for EMC expert evaluation of the equipment to be placed on the object in conditions of insufficient a priori information regarding the technical specifications of the radio systems, namely possible interference sources and receptors - the nonlinear sensor method implemented, specifically with the aid of the EMC prediction and analysis expert system «EMC-Analyzer». The main idea of this method consist in representation of radio receiver placed on the object in the form of simplified structural/functional model named nonlinear sensor model which have the main properties of the corresponding radio receiver path important from the EMC point of view (including main receiving channel sensitivity and selectivity, linear and nonlinear interference susceptibility), and consecutive analysis of electromagnetic environment and EMC analysis using nonlinear sensor model of receiver in different possible space points on object territory available for radio receiver antenna allocation. The main radio receiver EMC characteristics used for its nonlinear sensor model creating are main, intermediate, image and other incidental receiving channels linear selectivity and sensitivity, and input nonlinearity parameters (IP or dynamic ranges for different types of intermodulation) up to 25-th order. The mentioned model ensures the possibility of both linear and nonlinear EMC analysis on the object, including the intermodulation interference analysis to the 15-25 order with the dynamic range not poorer than 240-300 dB.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Antennas, in Which near Zone is Area of a Small Field
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Three types of small-sized unsuperdirective antennas designs are described, in which near zone there is an area with a small field. This area is formed as a result of mutual suppression of antenna various sections radiation. The electrodynamics calculation methods (analysis and synthesis) of such antennas are given. The antennas with “a dark spot” in a near zone are necessary for electromagnetic compatibility maintenance and for development of mobile telephones, which are not creating the large fields in the user's head location, i.e. ecologically harmless. The formation of “a dark spot” in a near zone does not distort the antenna pattern.

Author Keywords: “A dark spot” in an antenna near zone
Mutual suppression of antenna sections radiation

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Emissions of Integrated Circuits – Influence of Some External Working Conditions
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: To comply with the electromagnetic compatibility requirements the emissions level of ICs should be kept sufficiently low. For this purpose ICs designers and manufacturers as well as ICs users have to apply various preventive technical means. Several techniques of reduction of EM emissions levels are considered in the paper and their practical usefulness is shortly reviewed. The supplied information is based on published investigations results as well as on the own experiments.

articleTitle: Networking of EMC Society as Exemplified by Forum of Laboratories Implementing EU Electromagnetic Compatibility Directive
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents a project funded by European Commission under the Fifth Framework Programme. The project called Forum of laboratories implementing EU Electromagnetic Compatibility Directive FOR-EMC has been approved after one of the last calls for proposals. The FOR-EMC is co-ordinated by Institute of Logistics and Warehousing, Poznań, Poland and consists of EMC institutions from 20 countries. The laboratories work or - are in the process of - preparation to operate in the field of implementation of 89/336/EEC Directive. The paper presents the structure, aims and range of activities of FOR-EMC.

articleTitle: Wide-Band Evaluation of Transmission-Line On-Platform Antennas Using the MM-PO Hybrid Method with the Impedance Matrix Interpolation and Adaptive Sampling
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A hybrid moment method-physical optics (MM-PO) formulation combined with the impedance matrix interpolation and adaptive frequency sampling is employed for wide-band analysis of transmission-line on-platform antennas. The approach exploits advantages of the combined techniques leading to a highly efficient dedicated numerical modeling tool. Sample numerical results are given for transmission-line rectangular loop and inverted-L antennas.

articleTitle: Observed Characteristics of the Ball Lightning Depending on Various Observation Circumstance
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The data is represented as a multi-dimensional vector in a space of ball lightning properties and observation conditions. The influence of different conditions is considered. The paper was partially prepared under Russian Foundation for Basic Research support (project 00-02-16256).

articleTitle: Application Possibilities of Electroconductive Textiles as Architectural Electromagnetic Shields
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electroconductive textiles, which are produced in the Textile Research Institute in Łódź (nonwovens WOM-E and IG-NS), are characterized with electromagnetic fields (EMF) shielding properties - preferably their electric component. Attenuation effectiveness research has been carried out in the frequency range: 0.3 - 30 MHz, 99.2 MHz, 215 MHz, 621 MHz, 900 MHz and 2450 MHz. Effectiveness of WOM-E textile was from 15 dB to 27 dB depending on the frequency, and IG-NS textile from 20 dB to 36 dB. The analysis of EMF distribution in the environment of devices producing EMF in the high frequency range, enabled estimation of desired shielding effectiveness values within 10 - 40 dB.

articleTitle: Reduction of Impulsive Interference in Color Image Applications by Using Nonlinear Order Statistics Filters
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Usually the image or video data are degraded through the insufficient resolution ability caused sensor. Random noise also can significantly distort an image or video sequence quality. The paper presents an analysis of different non-linear filtering techniques used to suppress impulsive noise and preserve fine color image details. Directional processing, nonparametric approach and order statistics filters have been investigated in here. We also present a novel filtering scheme that can be able to decrease the noise influence by filtering of corrupted color image or video sequence and provide preservation of fine details. The before presented algorithm MM-KNN and another novel ones RM type filters (WM-KNN, ABSTM-KNN) have been adapted to color imaging and investigated in here. Such a RM-KNN filter can provide color detail preservation and uses the combination of the redescending M-estimators with one from median, Wilcoxon or two other designed estimator for KNN filter calculating the robust point estimate of the pixels within the filtering window and provide impulsive noise rejection.. We have applied in redescending M-estimator different influence functions: the simplest cut, Hampel's three part redescending, Andrew's sine, Tukey biweight, and Bernoulli ones. Several criteria used to compare the quality of image processing are very important to characterize the level of noise suppression obtained in each algorithm, edge, fine details preservation, and color perceptual, and chromaticity errors. Such the criteria were the Pick Signal Noise Relation (PSNR), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Normalized Color Difference (NCD), and Mean Chromaticity Error (MCRE). The analyzed algorithms have been implemented on DSP Texas Instruments DSP TMS320C6701 for proving the possibility to process an image in real time and to obtain the values of processing time when different intensity noise corrupts a color image or sequence.

articleTitle: Conducted EMI Propagation Modelling in the Wound Components
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The modelling of EMC behaviour of power electronics converters require specific models of devices which are adequate in a wide frequency range. A novel equivalent-circuit model of the inductor, suitable for EMC applications, has been developed and validated. The model can be used for the analyses of wounded components’ behaviour in the conducted-EMI frequency range. The parameters of the proposed model can be evaluated based on the selected impedance characteristic measurement.

articleTitle: Polarization of the Schumann Resonance Horizontal Magnetic Field in the Anisotropic Earth-Ionosphere Cavity
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We present the polarization characteristics of the horizontal magnetic field component in the Schumann resonance band (4-f0 Hz). The resonance is observed in the spherical Earth-ionosphere cavity driven by emission of the global thunderstorm activity. The upper boundary of the cavity in formed by the anisotropic plasma of the lower ionosphere, which is found in the geomagnetic field. The plasma anisotropy may cause a peculiar behavior of the resonance electromagnetic field. We treat the formal electromagnetic problem first and compute the expected impact of Earth 's magnetic field on the polarization of resonance waves. The simplest model is used of a single compact equatorial thunderstorm center that circles the planet during the day. In the second part of the report, we present durable experimental data on the polarization of the Schumann resonance fields. Finally, we compare the data computed with the experimental results and demonstrate their exceptional consistency. A conclusion is made that elliptic polarization of natural ELF radio signal around peak frequencies proves that there exists the splitting of the Schumann resonance lines caused by the geomagnetic field.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Influence of Interconnections on Switched Mode Power Electronics Systems by a Circuit Simulator Expanded with PEEC Models
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A new effective numerical tool for investigation of power electronic circuits is developed. It is a universal PEEC model of an arbitrary interconnection system incorporated in the circuit simulator SIMPLORER™ as an external module. This approach allows to analyze the influence of interconnections on transients in switching power electronic networks by numerical modeling with the help of SIMPLORER™ code. This approach is of interest for the EMC analysis and design in power electronics as well. The full bridge inverter built with MOSFETs is used for experimental verification of the numerical results. The results measured in the time domain show a good agreement with the simulation.

articleTitle: On a Possibility of Crosstalk-Free Propagation of Signals in Coupled Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with the problems of crosstalk reduction in multiconductor transmission lines. The fundamental properties of coupled lines are studied with aid of an electromagnetic simulator. This investigation leads to a conclusion that crosstalk elimination is possible even when different signals are transmitted through non-orthogonal sets of the line's modes. Practical circuit configurations with such properties are shown and reference to experimental verification of the effects is provided

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Hazards in the Workplaces - in the Light of Polish and EU Guidelines
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Analysis of electromagnetic fields (EMF) intensity levels has been carried out for data collected of more than 8000 devices used in five branches of national economy. Analysis of the above data demonstrated that 16% of the controlled devices failed to meet EU recommendations (i.e. ICNIRP’1998). In comparison, the national guidelines’ criteria were not met by 6.7% of devices. Because the adopted criteria in the above mentioned guidelines cannot be compared, exposure of workers has been estimated only according to the national guidelines’ criteria. The greatest exposure risk occurs in the vicinity of induction heaters, dryers and welders, electrosurgery, diathermy and near active antenna systems.

articleTitle: Theory and Numerical Simulation of the Internal EM Fields Excited by the External Source in the Cable Lines of Different Assignment
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The theoretical analysis and numerical simulation of effect of the external EM fields of a wide frequency range on cable lines of various assignment (including power transmission lines and information coaxial lines, i.e. radiofrequency cables) are presented. The problem is reduced to calculation of the internal diffraction field in extended cylindrical object having bedded structure with essentially distinguishing electrical and magnetic properties of layers, that can be further used for calculation of voltage and currents excited by this EM field and the distortions imported by the induced currents to a line, and the propagation of the current and voltage waves in a cable.

articleTitle: Interference Mitigation between Short-Range Wireless Systems: Bluetooth and IEEE 802.11B
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The article presents various ways of fighting the mutual interference effects between the Bluetooth and the IEEE 802.11b systems. The proposed solutions are categorized into collaborative and non-collaborative. An Adaptive Frequency Hopping technique is analyzed in greater detail, enumerating its advantages and drawbacks. Finally, solutions in the physical layer are suggested which, if used in combination with the MAC-layer AFH technique, could ensure optimal performance of both systems. It is also pointed out that the expected benefits of this hybrid solution would be applicable to many other indoor wireless systems, different from Bluetooth and IEEE 802.11b.

articleTitle: Coexistence of In-Home PLC and VDSL Systems
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a study of the impact of a PLC link on a VDSL transmission placed in the vicinity. Initially, the stationary noise generated by coupling on the telephone cable is measured for various distances of spacing from the power line. Then, the reductions in performance of a VDSL transmission in terms of rate related to the increase in stationary noise are calculated by simulation. It appears that for certain configurations, the performance of VDSL systems will be degraded.

articleTitle: Time Domain Modeling of Interconnected Integrated Circuits Based on Black Box Approach and Model Order Reduction for Signal Integrity Applications
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents black box based abstract approach to the modeling of the whole (driver, interconnect, receiver) signal path in high density packaged (HDP) integrated circuits (IC). As interconnected ICs constitute very complex systems, they require effective representation for system level simulations. Mathematical description of ICs and interconnects can deliver fast and compact time domain macromodels that are easy to implement in Spice. In this article simulation results of several black box ICs macromodels connected to model order reduced interconnect description are presented. These time domain macromodels allow for numerically efficient analysis and simulation of the signal behavior in interconnected, modern ICs.

articleTitle: Slot Antenna on a Paraboloid
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A field of a long line of convergent parabolical wires is determined. A problem of an electrostatic field account reduces to a planar one - to an account of two parallel filaments field. A capacitance per unit length and a wave impedance of a long line with convergent parabolical wires are calculated. By means of going from a symmetric V-shaped magnetic dipole to slot antenna an input impedance of a radiator located on a paraboloid surface and excited at its apex is determined. The radiator can be built of two metal filaments, or two volumetric metal tubes, or two metal shells. If the angular width of shells and slots between them are identical, they form a self-complementary antenna with constant (independent of frequency) and purely active input impedance.

articleTitle: Lithosphere Structure of Antarctica by the Satellite Data
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The complex analysis of outcomes of registration of low frequency noise emissions, variations intensity of flows miscellaneous energies electrons and temperature of ambient satellite plasma registered simultaneously onboard a low- altitude satellite "Intercosmos 19" is executed. The data are obtained in southern hemisphere above Antarctic Continent. By comparison of structural zones of lithosphere and measurements results of satellite parameters is established, that the variations of intensity of low frequency noise above deep faults are similarity to variation one above faults of Barents-Kara seas in northern hemisphere. The compare of lithosphere structure zones with observed datas of low energy (Ee~ 50 eV) and flows of middle energy (Ee≥ 40 keV and Ee ≥ 100 keV) electrons above faults Antarctic Continent has shown following. The tectonic borders (limit) of building blocks, introduced faults, find the reflection as well in bursts of miscellaneous energies electrons. The set (combination) of outcomes of our researches has demonstrated response of an ionosphere to slow geodynamic processes flowing past in lithosphere.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Electromagnetic Wave Scattering by Object Located near Water Surface
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The application of different kinds of passive nonlinear scatters (up and down-converting the soundind signal spectrum) to detection of object located near the water-air boundary is discussed. Preliminary investigation results in the decimeter waveband are given.

articleTitle: Suppression Method Study for Conducted EMI in PWM Adjustable Speed System
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper a new conducted EMI noise suppression method for PWM adjustable speed system is proposed based on analyzing the route and theory of conducted EMI. According to the differential coupling route and distributing of EMI source, the conducted EMI noise can be separated into two parts by the converter and suppressed by a current compensator and a common mode voltage canceller based on active filter. A new filter configuration is developed for the conducted EMI noise suppression based on the theoretical analysis. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by the experimental results.

articleTitle: Estimation of Spectrum Pricing for GSM Channels in Cases of Sharing Utilization Frequency Band for Radio Navigation and Land Mobile Services
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with economical aspects of Spectrum Management problems concerning the GSM-900 mobile networks and radio electronic equipment (REE) of the aeronautical radionavigation service (ARNS), were called RSBN/PRMG. Proposed by authors approach to estimation of spectrum pricing takes into account parameters of electromagnetic environment, radiated by RSBN and GSM networks. The value of GSM channels changes essentially depending on restrictions the radiation parameters of GSM network's base stations (BS). In that cases the equal spectrum pricing rate fixed by National Regulatory Authorities (NRA) for spectrum using of GSM channels is unfair judgment. Proposed by authors model allows to take into account variation of spectrum pricing for GSM channels, depending on restrictions for radiation that is defined by EMC RSBN and GSM systems. Proposed model guarantees proportional spectrum pricing rate according to value of GSM channel for network mobile operator in NRA spectrum management process.

articleTitle: Reduction of Narrowband Interference from Wideband CDMA Signals with Usage of Overcomplete Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with the method of narrowband interference rejection from wideband signal of IS-95 system. The solution is based on OWT (Overcomplete Wavelet Transform) and three step algorithm (decomposition, thresholding, reconstruction). New method of threshold calculation was also presented. It is based on CCDF (Complementary Cumulative Distribution Function) determined for wavelet coefficients.

articleTitle: Investigations on Induced Common Mode Voltages in Power Cables
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The protective earth conductor of power cables is usually grounded at several locations. Hence conductive loops are generated which consists of the protective earth conductor in the cable and of the structures of the equipotential bonding system to which the protective earth conductor is connected. The inductive coupling from the phase conductors into those loops causes common mode voltages in the protective earth system with consequent common mode currents. It is demonstrated that this effect takes place even in the case of balanced phase currents in a power cable and it can be explained by the relative asymmetry of the protective earth conductor arrangement with respect to the phase conductors. Hence this effect is particularly pronounced for power cables in which the protective earth conductor is twisted along with the phase conductors. Numerical simulations were performed for investigation of this effect from a quantitative point of view. Parameter studies are carried out in order to assess the impact of the different cable parameters on the common mode voltages. The simulations showed that common mode currents up to a few percent of the phase currents have to be taken into account.

articleTitle: Harmonization Procedures for Spectrum Management in Accession Countries
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In order to help in the process of setting out the Agency for Telecommunications in Serbia we have collected and analyzed the available data on the best practice in management and monitoring of the radio spectrum. Firstly, we give a general overview of the effective management of the radio spectrum and explain how different spectrum management techniques and tools can assist national objectives. Secondly, we discuss international framework for spectrum management. Finally, we present some data on spectrum monitoring and enforcement as the crucial activities in ensuring overall efficient spectrum management.

articleTitle: How to Destruct Tornadic Thunderstorms
