publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: New method for destructing tornadic thunderstorms are proposed based on electrohydrodynamics (EHD) with novel physical concepts of electric reconnection and critical ionization velocities as well as modern concepts of self-organizations and chaos

articleTitle: IEEE 802.11b Throughput Analysis in Presence of Bluetooth Interference
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper analysis and experimental results of the IEEE 802.11b system performance in typical household environment is presented. Number of experiments with Bluetooth devices as an interference sources are introduced. In this typical scenario interference measurements between Bluetooth and IEEE 802.11 devices and the system throughput are presented. In the paper negative effects of the interferences for the system performance are presented. Some analytical conclusions are also described.

articleTitle: Grounding System Characteristics While Lightning Strikes IT
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Grounding system characteristic during lightning strike isn’t constant. It depends on ground resistivity, surge current value, grounding network. Presented calculations show resonance phenomenon in grounding network.

articleTitle: EMC Simulation of Vehicle Radiocommunication Base Station
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents a complex EMC approach to design and electromagnetic modeling of multifunctional mobile antenna base station. Theoretical analyses of power parameters and operation modes of the vehicle antenna array are presented. A simulation of far and near electromagnetic fields of the broadband matched antenna station is excited.

articleTitle: Emerging Stratospheric Radio
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: New radiocommunication technologies, known as High Altitude Platform Stations (HAPS) or Stratospheric Platform Radio (SPR) are emerging. Predicted to operate commercially soon, they are expected to complement the “old” technologies and even replace some of them. They combine the benefits of terrestrial and satellite radio, promising access to modern telecommunication services at affordable price. With all promises fulfilled, these technologies would generate a multitude of new applications and services changing substantially the existing telecommunication businesses, wired and wireless, terrestrial, and satellite, as well as new electromagnetic compatibility problems. The paper presentation will be complemented by projection of short film.

articleTitle: Waveform Parameters of the Electromagnetic Pulse Generated by First and Subsequent Lightning Return Strokes to the CN Tower
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Since 1991 broadband high-resolution measurement systems have been in operation to simultaneously capture the lightning current derivative at the CN Tower and the lightning-generated electromagnetic pulse 2 km north of the Tower. Extensive statistics of the electric field waveform parameters of first and subsequent return strokes, generated by flashes to the Tower during an 11-year period (1992-2002), are derived. The presented analysis illustrates that the electric field waveform parameters of first return strokes are generally different from those of subsequent return strokes. The presented results will assist in the establishment of protective measures against the lightning electromagnetic pulses, especially those generated from lightning occurring at elevated objects.

articleTitle: Influence of UWB Signals on the Quality of Reception in GSM Mobile Stations
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with influence of UWB signals on the quality of reception in GSM mobile stations. It contains brief presentation of topics concerning UWB signal generation and propagation as well as limits put on the level of UWB emissions. The main part of the paper is focused on tests performed in the Institute of Radioelectronics. Obtained results are described and discussed.

articleTitle: Differential Effects of Centimeter and Millimeter Waves on Antibody in MICE
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Whole body microwave irradiation with low-intensity waves (8.15-18.00 GHz, 1 Hz within; and 40 GHz with 1 Hz amplitude modulation) caused the changes in plasma antibody concentration in immunized mice. The levels of primary and secondary immune responses were evaluated on the 15<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> and 30<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> day after prolonged daily irradiation. Additionally, T cell count was detected. 8.15-18.00 GHz microwave exposure significantly increased antibody production. In opposite, plasma antibody concentration in mice irradiated to 40 GHz decreased as compared to untreated animals. Our results suggest that centimeter microwaves can be use as a possible tool for the stimulation of immune system.

articleTitle: Global Positioning System Phase Fluctuations at Polar Ionosphere
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Dual-frequency measurements of the differential carrier phase of GPS: L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>= 1.575GHz) and L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>= 1.227GHz) signals have been used to study the development of phase fluctuations at Antarctic ionosphere during geomagnetic storms. The phase fluctuations of trans-ionospheric signals have been caused by the presence of large scale irregularities in the ionosphere. Observations from 5 stations at southern hemisphere provided possibility to study the instantaneous picture of the occurrence of the phase fluctuations during the storm. The storm-time features in longitude of phase fluctuations are discussed. The storm-time occurrences of polar patches are also presented.

articleTitle: Regulation of Radio Silence
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: To operate at their maximum sensitivity, radio astronomy stations require a “radio quiet” environment, i.e. where the interference received by the radio astronomy station concerned does not exceed the thresholds necessary for this station to operate at its maximum sensitivity. An instrument to achieve a radio quiet environment concerns regulatory provisions by the relevant national Administration that include specific criteria for the technical parameters of potentially interfering radio stations that are necessary to obtain these thresholds. In addition, based on these criteria a radio quiet area or zone could be a tool to mitigate the impact of transmitting radio stations while taking into account the specificities for terrestrial, aeronautical and space-based radio stations. A necessary basis for the development of such regulations are globally adopted regulatory provisions as outlined in the Radio Regulations of the International Telecommunication Union, ITU, and related ITU guidelines and documentation. National Administrations may use additional requirements and develop additional regulation to protect a specific site within its territory. A new generation of international radio astronomy telescopes is being designed and under construction that will be about a hundred times more sensitive than present instruments, and which will have observational capabilities over a very wide range of radio frequencies, well exceeding the bands allocated to radio astronomy. To facilitate their scientific and operational objectives, these telescopes will be built in remote areas where the radio environment may offer better protection for radio astronomical observations from ground-based interference. Remoteness of a new generation radio telescope may not be sufficient to achieve a radio quiet environment. This contribution gives a preliminary view on this issue, inter alia on regulatory and legal aspects related with the establishment of a radio quiet environment for these instruments, specifically if international radio quiet zones are considered. Precedents for an international radio quiet zone are examined in view of their relevance for the new generation of radio telescopes. Finally, this contribution lists some considerations on regulatory and legal elements that could be relevant for the establishment of an international radio quiet zone.

articleTitle: Novel Interpretation for the Spectra of Ionospheric Alfven Resonance
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Ionospheric Alfven resonance (IAR) is observed in the terrestrial radio noise from ultra low (ULF) to extremely low frequencies (ELF). Spectral peaks detected are traditionally related to Alfven waves captured in the ionosphere - magnetosphere plasma. The resonance pattern is observed at the ground, and its source is not established conclusively: many types of driving mechanisms for AIR oscillations were discussed in literature. We suggest a novel interpretation for the resonance spectra. The mechanism involves only electromagnetic waves propagating through the plasma. Spectral peaks appear without premise of Alfven or any other plasma waves trapped in the ionosphere: they originate in the traveling radio wave owing to the well-known interaction of partial reflections from the upper and lower interfaces of the ionosphere. Such a mechanism, although never applied to explain IAR, describes all experimental results. Additional investigations are required to prove that IAR signals are linked to the trapped plasma waves.

articleTitle: Radio Devices Database in the Frequency Management
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper describes methodology which can be used in order to collect and refine the radio devices data required in the EMC assessment carried out for microwave links.

articleTitle: EM Radiation from Hydrocarbonic Plasmoid, Modeling Ball Lightning, as an Activator of Water Solutions
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The investigation of useful properties of highpower plasmoid described at previous Wroclaw EMC conference is continued. The new approach to the ecological environmental problems is proposed. It is founded on the electromagnetic radiation from the hydrocarbonic plasmoid. The peculiarity of the new method is an activation of organically (and non-organically ) contaminated water solutions through the material of the vessel. The rapidness of activation (decontamination) of polluted liquid is a strong point of the investigated method. The diagnostic procedures and theoretical modeling of energy transfer in atmosphere are discussed.

articleTitle: EHD for Electrobiology and its Applications to Cancer Treatment and Life Elongation
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: While conventional biology is primarily based on molecular biology and hence more recent interest in electromagnetic effects on biological matter termed ‘electrobiology’ is also based on cell or molecule description for microstructure, in contrast continuum (fluid) description for macrostructure based on ‘electrohydrodynamics (EHD)’ has been developed and applied to cancer treatment and life elongation by the present authors and their highlights are described in this paper.

articleTitle: FDTD Simulation Modelling for Electrostatic Discharge Immunity Test
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: ESD (Electrostatic discharge) testing is becoming an essential item to test the immunity of electronic and information equipment. As a powerful tool for taking effective ESD countermeasures in the early design stage of electronic products, we previously developed a finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) proto-type model for the contact discharge of a commercially available ESD-gun with specification of the IEC61000-4-2 standard. We validated its effectiveness comparing the simulated discharge current for the contact discharge to a 50-Ohm SMA connector with the measured result, although only the simple skeleton structure of the ESD-gun was modeled in the proto-type. In the present study, we improved the previous FDTD modeling to realize a more realistic ESD-gun for accurate simulation, and examined the effects of the structure modeling and the plastic covering used in the gun on ESD simulation. As a result, we found that the precise structure modeling of the ESD-gun gives good agreement of the contact discharge simulation with the measurement, while the covering does not almost affect the simulation. With the improved FDTD model, we then simulated the ESD testing for a printed circuit board (PCB) with a finite ground plate. A 50- Ohm micro-strip line fabricated on the PCB was modeled, and was excited in contact to the sending end with the ESD-gun. We found that there is good agreement between the simulation and the measurement for the induced voltages appearing in the receiving end of the micro-strip line.

articleTitle: Observation of Sprites over the Sea of Japan and Conditions for Lightning-Induced Sprites in Winter
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We have succeeded in observing sprites for winter lightning in the Hokuriku area (Japan Sea side) of Japan in the winter of 2001/2002. Despite significant differences of Hokuriku winter lightning from the summer-time continental lightning, we have found nearly the same sprite properties as already observed in the U.S. continent with significant differences (simpler shape for Hokuriku winter sprite). Then, we have also discussed the criteria for sprite occurrence. Specifically, two similar criteria are found: (1) cloud-to-ground discharges of positive polarity and (2) the presence of a certain threshold in vertical charge moment change (200-300C'km)(roughly consistent with that for the U.S. continent). Mesoscale convective systems are not necessary to store the charge necessary for sprites, but the parent Hokuriku winter clouds are substantially smaller than the minimum scale for sprite occurrence in the continental lightning. There may exit another condition such as clustering or self-organizing effect of thunderclouds for sprite production.

articleTitle: Review of Simple Electromagnetic Models for Predicting Radiated Emissions from PCBS
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper reviews the basic mechanisms through which voltage and current signals in printed circuit boards (PCBs) produce unwanted radiated emissions and some analytical models that can be used to predict these radiated emissions. Three models are applied to a simple PCB and the results are compared to those obtained with the electromagnetic analysis carried out with a Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) computer code. Although the models are not likely applicable to real-life problems, the comparison is useful to underline their assumptions and limitations.

articleTitle: CATV Leakage Measurements at Heights
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents the example results of the CATV leakage measurements at heights, the correlation between those results and measurements done inside buildings. It also describes an automatic leakage measurement system with a GPS receiver which can be useful also for coverage measurements of analog and digital broadcasting systems.

articleTitle: Investigation of Resolution Enhancement in Near-Field Scanning
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In order to improve on the resolution and accuracy of measurements obtained by electromagnetic near-field scans a calibration method based on deconvolution is proposed. The influence of magnitude-only as well as magnitude and phase measurement on the deconvolution efficiency is discussed and compared to standard calibration. Results are given for the electric field component normal to the DUT area and compared with simulation. The used monopole probe was calibrated according to the standard, allowing to quantitatively evaluate the DUT. The proposed method much improves the resolution of the measured field component and gives accurate results in the areas of its dominant emission level.

articleTitle: Waves in GTEM Cells - A Combined Analytical - Numerical Approach
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The analysis is based on an ansatz for the Hertzian vector potential in spherical coordinates and components followed by a numerical solution of a 2D differential equation. The conditions for coupling and decoupling of modes for perfectly conducting walls as well as for boundary conditions described by a wall impedance concept are discussed.

articleTitle: DE-Noising the CN Tower Lightning Current Derivative Signal Using Short Term Fourier Transform-Based Spectral Subtraction
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The CN Tower is a transmission tower and it is not unexpected that recorded lightning current signals be corrupted by noise. The existence of noise may affect the calculation of current waveform parameters (current peak, 10-90% risetime to current peak, maximum steepness, and pulse width at half value of current peak). To determine accurate statistics of current waveform parameters, the interfering noise must be removed. In this paper, a Short Term Fourier Transform (STFT)-based Spectral Subtraction method is developed to denoise the lightning current derivative signal measured at the CN Tower. In order to evaluate the proposed de-noising method, a simulated current derivative waveform is used after being artificially distorted by a noise signal measured at the CN Tower in the absence of lightning. The de-noised waveform proved to be very close to the original simulated waveform. The STFT-based Spectral Subtraction method is then applied successfully to de-noise the lightning current derivative signal recorded at the CN Tower. A signal peak-to-noise peak ratio (SPNPR) of the lightning current signal is defined and calculated before and after the de-noising procedure.

articleTitle: Modeling and Extraction of Inductances on Chip Level
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The modelling and simulation of magnetic interactions on chip level has become more and more important in the last years. This is due to smaller structures and as well as rising clock frequencies. This contribution should give an overview on the analysis of parasitic inductances. It should also show their influence on the functional behaviour and the thus resulting design measures. The main problem during the extraction of parasitic on chip inductances is the fact that an inductance the function of a closed current loop. Therefore it is necessary to analyse the complete current path. It consists of signal path and current return path via the power supply system or substrate. Thus the current distribution of the whole circuit has to be known for getting correct indications on the loop inductance. Beside the geometrical structures it depends on parameters like decoupling capacitors, rise and fall times and clock frequencies. Consequently the extraction of the current path and therefore also the inductance results as a non trivial problem. Within this contribution the basic principles and mechanisms for the extraction of on chip inductances will be presented. Furthermore the dedicated inductance extraction for dynamic current analyses and the resulting design measures will be shown.

articleTitle: Structure and Computer Modeling of Mobile Base Station of Radiocommunication Systems
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents structure and EMC modeling of multifunctional mobile base station of the radiocommunication system. Several modes of the base station and results of design and computer simulation of hybrid phase commutator are described. Results of experimental investigation of the antenna array are represented.

articleTitle: Propagation Reliability of Line-of-Sight Radio Relay Systems above 10 GHz
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The total unavailability of radio links systems is the sum of the probability of hardware failure and unavailability due to propagation conditions. It is mainly propagation features that cause unavailability in systems operating in the frequency bands above 10 GHz. This paper covers unavailability due to propagation phenomena. At National Institute of Telecommunications (NIT) the radio links have been developed to test propagation in band X, Ka and Q. This paper describes the example test results of wave attenuation in above mentioned radio links.

articleTitle: Standardisation and PLC, State of the Art
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, we propose a state of the art of the standardisation related to broadband power line communication. All the standardisation bodies and the associated relations are defined. Both network and product standards are exposed. We focus also on CE marking and the applications of the EMC directive.

articleTitle: Peculiarities of Measuring Low-Frequency Magnetic Fields in Moving Objects Closed Electrically
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Investigations of biological influence of electromagnetic fields on human organism situated in an electrically closed moving object with many own electromagnetic field sources are not developed sufficiently. The orbital space station and the passenger car cabin can be considered as examples of electrically closed moving objects, in which a man is influenced by nearly situated radiation sources. Also the problem of comparison of the measured values of electromagnetic field components strength with the approved normative documentation which regulate the permissible field levels from the point of view of their safety influence exists. The problem of measurement in the mentioned conditions consists in the fact that radiating sources are situated near a person, i.e. an operator is situated in the near zone of the source (in the induction field). Manifestation of magnetic field biological activity depends on mutual location of a radiation source and a radiated object, on distance between them, on presence of objects that can reflect or shield electromagnetic fields, and on using ground connection, that is usually used when operators work in electrically closed objects. The information-measuring system "Kaskad" are described in the report and some results of magnetic field investigation on the board of the "Mir" space station and in some types of cars are presented.

articleTitle: Simple Method for Evaluation of the near Field of the GSM Base-Station Antennas
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The simple and effective method for evaluation of near field of the cellular telephony base-station antennas is presented in this paper. The method bases on the replacement of panel antenna with a discrete array. Obtained approximate results have been compared with those calculated by using the moment method. Excellent agreement has been obtained.

articleTitle: Features of Antenna Theory Models of Lightning Return Stroke
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Adaptations of antenna theory for the modelling of the lightning return stroke are discussed in the present paper. These models are convenient for the LEMP action analysis performed with the help of commonly used antenna software. The characteristic features that are essential for engineering computations are discussed.

articleTitle: Analysis of Polarization Effects on Wave Penetration INTO an Enclosure with Aperture Using FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Nowadays, the problem of electromagnetic waves penetration and interference is one of the most challenging discussions considered by many EMC experts. Admittedly, the development of modern science and technology that has led to an increasing usage of high sensitivity electronic instruments, is one of the most effective factors in making the problem of protection such crucial. It's predictable that future interest will tend to find shielding strategies that are not only efficient and reliable but also simple and inexpensive. However, introducing an appropriate shielding scheme, proper for a specific situation, may not be achieved unless a rigorous investigation in wave penetration mechanism is performed. In this paper, the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method along with a new implementation of perfectly matched layer (PML) is used to investigate the wave penetration mechanism into a metallic enclosure with a rectangular aperture in one wall. The suggested strategy for PML implementation results in a great ease in computer implementation and makes the possible future geometrical changes to be applied very easily. For example, a 1200-line program can be written in just 300 lines using this strategy. The geometry under consideration is an aluminum container with a 8.4×3.6cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> aperture in one wall. The thickness of each wall is assumed to be 0.6 cm and the FDTD space is divided into 90 × 80 × 80(= 576000) cubic cells and the cell size is taken to be 0.6 cm. The incident wave is a uniform sinusoidal plane wave with amplitude 100 V/m and frequency 300 MHz, which impinges perpendicularly to the wall of the container and penetrates into it through the aperture. The effects of two different polarizations are studied. Some useful protection strategies are suggested and the corresponding improvements are investigated. Finally, the validation of applied modeling is verified by comparing the results with the reported works.

articleTitle: Study of Possible Far Field EMI Impacts through High Speed Power Line Communication
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: If the impact of unwanted radiated HF signals from Powerline Communication (PLC) Systems to the far field has to be investigated, the assumption of field strength decreasing proportional to 1/r is common practice in many theoretical studies. However, the standard measuring distance is r<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> = 3 m, so far field conditions are not met over a great portion of the relevant spectrum from 1.5 to 30 MHz. As the power supply grid is a very complex environment, reliable data can only be obtained from detailed measurements, which are not yet available with a sufficient statistical basis. This paper first reviews some simulation results for propagation to the far field and, in the main part, concentrates on the experimental verification of the 1/r approximation for field strength depending on distance.

articleTitle: Research of Electromagnetic Influence of Traction Current and its Harmonics on the Rail Circuits
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The experimental investigation of interference in rail net at the supply railway section of d. c. power and modeling of 50 Hz harmonics distribution on a length of feeder zone were done. The measuring method for the definition spectrum composition of traction current is proposed.

articleTitle: HF-Shielding of a GPS Antenna System
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: On modern military ships more and more low cost COTS (Commercial off the shelf) equipment is installed in the upper deck area. Their immunity against high frequency electromagnetic fields is only specified with 10 V/m. Military components on the other hand are specified with 200 V/m. With the multitude of transmission-antennas and high HF- power, there is nearly no place at upper deck on modern ships, where the fieldstrength is durable under 10 V/m and the COTS equipment can work interference-free. The highest fieldstrength on naval ships are produced in the HF-Area from 1.5 MHz up to 30 MHz. In this frequency range the Transmitters on board have an output power of about 1000 Watts up to 1500 Watts. The wavelength is between 200 m (at 1.5 MHz) and 10 m (at 30 MHz). In most facts the power of the transmitters and so the field- strength at the location of the COTS-components could not be reduced because of preconditions from the customer However the COTS-components have to be protected against the high frequency field without impairing there function.

articleTitle: Errors in Vertically-Polarized Site Attenuation Measurements Due to Externally-Induced Antenna Imbalance
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Errors in vertically-polarized site attenuation measurements are addressed with emphasis on those due the externally-induced imbalance due to the presence of the ground plane. The interaction between the antenna, the balun, and the feed structure are considered by employing 3-terminal, 2-port antenna models and 3-port balun models. It is shown that, of the fundamental balun types, the current balun is the most appropriate for such site attenuation measurements. However, it is also shown that the SA that would be measured using antennas with ideal current baluns still differs from that predicted by a model utilizing antennas with self-contained sources.

articleTitle: Wide Band Data Transsmision Equipment Regulatory and Proprietary Requirements & Standards
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Across the world a communications revolution is quietly under way. Radio LANs are becoming a more and more important form of wireless communications where high bit-rates are needed over a relatively short distance. They are being deployed globally both for public and private use. With wireless LAN technology expecting rapid growth, coexistence issues between different classes of wireless devices have become a significant topic of analysis and discussion.

articleTitle: The Monitoring Earth Station at Leeheim, Germany
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The Monitoring Earth Station at Leeheim, Germany, is a tool supporting the technical regulation competence of the RegTP. Its main tasks are, firstly, to assist frequency planning and spectrum engineering, secondly, to monitor orbit and frequency occupation in order to know whether regular satellites operate as advance published, coordinated or notified internationally, or to identify unknown or “paper” satellites, and, thirdly, to handle interference of space radio services. The Station's three presently operational antennas cover, except of some gaps, the frequency range from 130 MHz to 12,75 GHz. They are azimuth elevation suspended. The fourth xy-suspended antenna, presently under construction, will, without gaps, cover the range from 1000 MHz to 26,5 GHz, i.e. the Station will, from the 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> quarter 2004 onwards, facilitate monitoring of the whole range from 130 MHz until 26,5 GHz. The fact, that the major receive bands will be then available twice, is a prerequisite to locate unknown transmitters on Earth by means of triangulation via two satellites. The Station can measure emission characteristics such as radio frequency, Doppler shift, bandwidth, power flux density, EIRP, and can identify polarisation of radio waves, class of emission, type of modulation and orbital elements of any satellite viewed at Leeheim. At the Station new monitoring methods are developed to measure emissions received approximately 15 dB below the noise floor to protect e.g. the radio astronomy service. Other services dealt with are the fixed, mobile, broadcasting, earth exploration and navigation satellite services as well as space research radio services and the inter-satellite service. Customers of the Station are entities within RegTP, satellite operators under German jurisdiction, national satellite users and radio astronomers, international members of a memorandum of understanding, i.e. foreign authorities, and an international satellite operator on contractual basis. The number of given tasks show the need for such a Station even in an environment of growing deregulation.

articleTitle: EMC Design Methodology for Microelectronic Systems
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Due to increased clock speeds (10 GHz) and data transfer rates (40 GBit/s) in the entire microelectronics area (partly also MEMS) arises an increasing demand for the efficient treatment of parasitic effects in the complete design process of microelectronic systems. In the future, no distinction between time and frequency response will exist (fT up to 110 GHz). I.e. digital, analogue design and RF design will grow together. In terms of high packing density, the different physical interferences (electronically-thermal-mechanical) have to be treated concurrently. These interferences have to be accounted for all along the design flow, starting from the early design stages, while refining the modelling and the simulation accuracy. The approach to improve EMC shall be related with other measures to improve signal-integrity (SI), robustness, functionality, power strategies, ESD, etc. to assure an integral system solution to optimally use intrinsic silicon capabilities. In the following some thoughts regarding the future development of EDA solutions which were made in the frame of the compilation of the MEDEAplus EDA Roadmap [7] are explained. It is considered the development of EDA solutions in the area Parasitic Extraction, Modeling and Analysis for the timeframe 2003 to 2008. This chapter of the MEDEAplus EDA Roadmap arose in the the years 2002/2003. In this contribution the thoughts regarding the MEDEAplus EDA Roadmap concentrate on the aspects: • EMC/SI and RF System Design with Respect to Parasitic Effects • Challenge of Packaging Technologies • Design to Noise Margin.

articleTitle: EMC Support Features for Digital TV Broadcasting Systems in DVB-T Standard and for Systems of Radar and Radar Navigation Services in the Frequency Band of 790-862 MHZ
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Paper propose the radio system protection criterions of the air navigation service and air traffic control service, in particular landing radio system through the development of the timed digital broadcasting networks in DVB-T standard. The results of critical analysis of the radio system protection rate of the air radar system which has been used in The Chester 1997 Multilateral Coordination Agreement relating to Technical Criteria, Coordination Principles and Procedures for the introduction of Terrestrial Digital Video Broadcasting (DVB-T) are given. Regulations of the distance separation for the transmitters in DVB-T standard and the air navigation service and the air traffic control service as a result of intersystem EMC analysis are presented. The conclusion that the admissible interference level for the RSBN systems must be no more than 28-32 dBμV/m within the frequency band of 770-812,8 MHz and no more than -5 dBμV/m within the frequency band 833.5-866 MHz.

articleTitle: Stellar Structure Corrected for Plasma-Body Radiation
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the previous papers [1]-[6] it was shown that Planck's radiation law has to be generalized in a homogeneous and isotropic plasma in thermal equilibrium and some consequences were investigated. A new parameter a = ħω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> /k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</inf>T occurs, where ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ρ</inf> is the angular plasma frequency and ħ, k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</inf> and T have their customary meaning. It should be stressed that there is no new principle involved: the generalization is entirely based on the combination of the well established dispersion relation for photons in a plasma and quantum statistics. Obviously when a tends to zero Planck's law is recovered. The increase in radiation energy by about 18 % ( a = 0.25 ) in the centre of the Sun requires the central temperature to decrease by 1.9%, i.e. 280, 000 K if T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> = 15 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> K. This decrease is relevant for neutrino production and thus for the solar neutrino experiments.

articleTitle: Methodology of Spectrum Monitoring Network Planning
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A newly developed methodology for spectrum monitoring network planning and optimization in V/UHF frequency bands is described. It is based on calculation of fixed monitoring station coverage areas in fulfillment of two major monitoring functions: distant measurement of emission parameters such as frequency, bandwidth, modulation, field strength etc. (measurements in accordance with Recommendations of the International Telecommunication Union, so-called “ITU measurements”) and location by triangulation operation. Propagation model and set of network planning parameters are proposed. A new tool for calculation of sets of location coverage zones, called “location coverage templates”, with known location accuracies, is developed. Their analysis is presented in the separate paper of the authors at the same EMC WROCLAW 2004.

articleTitle: Modern Radio Spectrum Management and Monitoring Challenges within the Context of the Recent European Regulation
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Among the recent European regulatory measures to support innovative electronic networks and services, there are specific initiatives for the co-ordination of radio spectrum policies, (especially within the context of the latest Decision No.676/2002). Frequency availability, spectrum efficient use and management are dynamic modules of the European economy and affect the successful transition towards an "Information Society for All citizens ", both corporate and residential. The paper discusses some amongst the major regulatory innovations and challenges, to ensure appropriate harmonised conditions for common approaches among all EU Member States. The work also overviews current EU priority issues for various frequency-based innovations, fundamental for further market evolution (also including the perspective for secondary trading of spectrum to achieve greater flexibility as for spectrum management), technology development and social cohesion, in parallel with international activities within the scope of WRC and summarizes with major concluding remarks and expectations for the future.

articleTitle: An Overview of Spectrum Management in India for new Telecommunication Services
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In early 1990s, the Indian economic policy makers realized that the future economic growth of the country would largely depend on its improved competitiveness in the global market along with rapid growth in exports. It was also visualized in the National Economic Plan 1991 that to achieve the expected growth, one of the major factors would be availability of the contemporary world class telecommunication services in the country. Therefore, development and expansion of the telecommunication services needed higher priority. Accordingly, National Telecom Policy 1994 (NTP94) was drafted. NTP94 had setup national targets for achieving universal access of basic telecom services and also for proliferation of value-added telecom services of international level. In order to meet economic resources required to achieve telecom infra-structure expansion goals, NTP94 proposed migration from monopolistic (incumbent) operator model to private sector participation in telecom services. It was felt that such reforms would introduce competitiveness among operators and increase availability of contemporary telecom services at competitive price to the end user. In view of the constraints on the availability of frequency spectrum for Cellular Mobile Telephone Services (CMTS), a policy of operator selection for the grant of licenses through competitive bidding was also framed in NTP94. Various agencies, like Telecom Regularity Authority of India (TRAI) and Telecom Dispute Settlement Appellant Tribunal (TDSAT), were also formed in late 1990s for recommending new telecom regulations to the Government through open consultation process and for early telecom dispute settlements. Based on the market feedback on the implementation of NTP94, and realizing the need of more effective private participation in developing Indian telecom infrastructure, New Telecom Policy 1999 (NTP99) was framed. Major features of the NTP99 include migration from heavy entry fee for spectrum user operators to annual revenue sharing with the operator. NTP99 also recommended revision of National Frequency Allocation Plan (NFAP) every two years, within ITU-region 3 framework, to account for the requirements of introducing new spectrum efficient technologies and protecting existing users. Wireless Planning Coordination Committee (WPCC) has been responsible for the development of NFAP. Presently, the Indian spectrum is governed by NFAP2002. An interministerial Standing Advisory Committee for Frequency Allocation (SACFA) decides the final site clearance for frequency use by the operator. SACFA has also been reformed over the years. Presently, the licensing period is 20 years, which can be extended up to additional 10 years. Recently, India has adopted unified licensing policy. Extension of spectrum license period incentive, in case of merger/acquisitions of operators, has also been permitted since 2004. With the increase in the subscriber base of an operator in a circle, additional bandwidth can be granted to an operator in small chunks on need by need basis. Such reforms in telecom policies have made the system flexible enough to adopt new technologies easily and respond to market forces with minimum intervention from the Government. This has helped expansion of national telecom networks at reasonable rates and benefit end users to get better telecom services at competitive price.

articleTitle: Improved EMC System Design for Microelectronic Applications
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Semiconductor manufacturers continuously provide faster, more cost effective and more highly integrated devices. By the end of the decade, clock frequencies are expected to be in the range of 10 GHz and design dimensions will have been reduced to 45 nm compared with 130 nm today. Chip area and component density will have increased with edge lengths in the range of 40 mm in comparison of 20 mm today. With such changes in performance and complexity, the issues of electromagnetic compatibility and parasitic emissions become ever more significant. In this paper a coherent approach to overcoming these problems at both chip and high-density packaging levels in the frame of the MEDEA+ project called MESDIE (Microelectronic EMC System Design for High Density Interconnect and High Frequency Environment - A509) will be presented. The introduction of new submicron technology and higher packaging density on the subsystem level has led to greater customer demand for high-quality semiconductor devices. Semiconductor manufacturers and their application customers now have to deal with constraints on the chip level to meet electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) requirements of systems and subsystems and are therefore searching for suitable solutions. Due to continuous miniaturisation, higher clock frequencies, faster edge rates and more functionalities, the electromagnetic emission (EME) problem is causing more and more trouble for semiconductor manufacturers in various application areas, such as these in automotive, multimedia, telecommunications and computing facilities. Satisfactory EMC microelectronic system designs that eliminate electromagnetic interference in electronic systems and an appropriate design methodology for integrated circuits (ICs) are crucial. Therefore methods and tools for an improved system design taking into account the boundary conditions and appropriate integration into design processes will be a major challenge for the global electronics industry in this decade. In order to achieve higher performance, microelectronic components and subsystems are moving towards ever increasing miniaturisation. This requires improved functionality of the substrate and high density interconnect (HDI)/high density packaging (HDP), as well as the integration of passive elements, EMC protection devices and optimized interconnect systems. As wiring demands and density increase, high density interconnect structures become an essential requirement for wire ability. This can be handled by either the use of new packaging strategies - such as system in package (SiP). Modelling is an important feature which brings together the semiconductor manufacturers, systems houses and R&D institutes with different backgrounds in technology and design methodologies to develop a common strategy on handling radio-frequency, EMC and susceptibility issues (EMC/RF/SI). The modelling aspects have to be handled on three levels: • electromagnetic emissions of IC • susceptibility at chip level and • new high-density interconnect structures. Therefore new approaches are necessary for modelling and simulation of radiation and susceptibility at chip level and new high density interconnect structures to deal with electromagnetic parasites simultaneously on both chip and high-density packaging levels. In addition, tool environment and design flows, rule development, diagnosis and validation on chip and HDP/HDI levels, as well as testing issues, such as the characterization of chip and HDP/HDI parameters have to be covered. To meet these challenges, the following tasks have to be fulfilled: • close the gap between IC-level design and application in terms of new hierarchical system design approaches and high density interconnect technology • achieve higher performance and more compact electronic equipment in relevant applications, such as automotive, telecommunications and consumer electronics • obtain a design methodology for the information network-based society of the future. Parasitic electromagnetic effects - such as reflections and crosstalk on interconnects, delta-I-noise within the power supply system, the threat of electrostatic discharge and ambient pollution by electromagnetic fields - have to be considered all in the design process together with conventional design constraints.

articleTitle: Fundamentals of National Spectrum Management
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper outlines the basic “Fundamentals of National Spectrum Management” as described in various Handbooks of ITU R Study Group 1 on Spectrum management. The paper describes the Goals, the Radio Laws, the National Allocation Table, National Spectrum Management Requirements, National Spectrum Fees, Radio Standards, Monitoring, International Cooperation and Spectrum Management Organizational Structures.

articleTitle: Improved EMC Support of Microelectronic Application Design by a Web Based Training System
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Today, the design of IC, subsystems and systems dealing with electromagnetic problems (EMC) is often based on insufficient data and on assumptions of design constraints. The term EMC (Electromagnetic Compatibility) includes, as generally might be known, all actions intended to eliminate electromagnetic interference in electronic systems. Growing complexity, denser design and higher clock rates all lead to a substantial increase in EMC problems and design time. EMC is not commonly accepted in microelectronic design. Microelectronic designers are the opinion that EMC has to do with electrical and electronic systems and mandatory product regulations instead of requirements to the integrated circuit they are designing. Therefore, design under EMC-constraints is a big challenge and requires highly skilled engineers. The high processing speeds and integration densities lead to effects like reflections, crosstalk on transmission lines, delta-I-noise (ground bounce, simultaneous switching, current spike) as well as to electromagnetic radiation and irradiation, which have to be considered when applying microelectronic components. Due to the package complexity of systems and components not all EMC-effects can be observed during the development process by measurement. Furthermore, measurement techniques for EMC analysis are greatly limited by engineering and financial constraints. Besides the consideration of international and national standards, of legal and company internal requirements, considering EMC-constraints in the development of electronic products becomes vital for quality and time to market. Due to the complexity of the basic physical theory and the transformation into design methods and tools there is a lack of practical training material which is accepted by industry. In this contribution a problem specific net based training system applied to signal integrity analysis on printed circuit boards will be introduced and presented. The training system gains its particular relevance within the actual frame of life long learning (L3) initiatives. It will also be pointed out that for employing new development strategies and environments most effectively, an adequate training system can be introduced in parallel

articleTitle: Numerical EM Field Modeling in EMC - Current and Future Developments
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper provides an overview of the three main research streams in numerical field modeling techniques. A selection of mainly time domain approaches is discussed and their current and future developments are highlighted. While one group of researchers is focusing on improving existing techniques within their given framework, another is trying to hybridize methods, that is to combine two or more different techniques to utilize only their advantageous feature and eliminate their disadvantages. A third but increasingly attractive research direction is to investigate model order reduction techniques (MOR). MOR aims at significantly reducing the dimension of the original model's state-space while preserving its port behavior, at least in a certain frequency range. The result is a model of significantly smaller size, which can be much better used for the extraction of system properties, equivalent circuit generation, fast frequency sweep, or circuit level simulation.

articleTitle: Spectrum Congestion and Interference Management
publicationTitle: 17th International Wroclaw Symposium and Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The concept of spectrum congestion has found its way into frequency management in spite of the fact that it is ill defined and used in a confusing manner. Spectrum congestion limits the development of all applications of radio and has significant economic impact. These limitations are particularly experienced by passive radiocommunication services. Transmissions from non-licensed devices contribute in a very specific way significantly to spectrum congestion. Spectrum congestion is also increased by transmissions at frequencies, at which no allocation for the service under which the application is operated, exists. Especially the impact of power line transmissions and of ultra-wide band technology are mentioned since recent studies by European Administrations have indicated that such applications can be incompatible with several radiocommunication services: such applications can be very hazardous to passive services and, therefore, these applications do increase spectrum congestion. Enabling radio facilities that do increase the noise floor and generate interference to some radiocommunication services raises the issue of “interference management” which is contrary to frequency management with the aim to prevent radio interference. On the other hand, the situation of frequency bands allocated to a relatively large number of different services leads to the impression of spectrum congestion, even if they are hardly used at all. Comments on spectrum congestion are made from the perspectives of technological development, administrative possibilities, commercial constraints and quality of operation of radiocommunication services. Some possible attractive solutions to reduce spectrum congestion, are evaluated in view of their impact on other radiocommunication services with their specific protection requirements and technologies. This contribution addresses the applicability of the tool of radio regulations and standards development to handle spectrum congestion while taking into account the interests of all radiocommunication services, including the most vulnerable ones, from the perspective of the passive services. Technical measures that could be used to reduce spectrum congestion could be proper filtering of signals unwanted by a (potential) victim service and efficient spectrum modulation. Avoidance of spectrum congestion is beneficial to all users of the radio frequency spectrum.
